landing.faq.what_is.question: What is CurvG AI, and how does it use Manim?
landing.faq.what_is.answer: CurvG is an AI math animation maker built on Manim Community, the open-source Python engine behind 3Blue1Brown-style math animation. It turns a written explanation goal into a scene plan and Manim code, with a review step before rendering.
landing.faq.installation.question: Do I need Python, FFmpeg, or LaTeX installed locally?
landing.faq.installation.answer: No — rendering runs in the cloud, so you can plan, generate, and render without installing anything. You only need a local Manim environment if you want to run the exported code on your own computer.
landing.faq.editing.question: Can I edit and compile the generated Manim code in the browser?
landing.faq.editing.answer: Not yet. The current Creator lets you view, copy, and download generated Python, but it does not provide direct code editing or compilation in the browser.
landing.faq.free.question: Can I use CurvG AI for free?
landing.faq.free.answer: Yes. New accounts start with free credits, and the Free plan includes scene planning, Manim code export, and three curated AI models (Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5, and Gemini 3.1 Pro). Pro unlocks all seven models.
landing.faq.difference.question: How is CurvG different from a one-click AI video generator?
landing.faq.difference.answer: CurvG does not stop at a prompt and a final video. It shows the proposed explanation, mathematical assumptions, scene order, and generated Manim code, so you can catch a problem before rendering. AI output is still not guaranteed to be correct.
landing.faq.accuracy.question: Can AI guarantee a mathematically correct animation?
landing.faq.accuracy.answer: No. A model can misread notation, make a false assumption, or generate incorrect scene logic. CurvG makes those decisions easier to inspect, but it does not replace mathematical review.
landing.faq.rendering.question: Can CurvG render the video for me?
landing.faq.rendering.answer: Yes. Cloud rendering is built in: approve the scene, render it to an MP4, and download the result. Paid plans include render credits, and failed or canceled renders are refunded automatically.

landing.pricing.faq.title: What to expect before you upgrade
landing.pricing.faq.description: A short, factual guide to Free, Starter, Pro, generated code, billing, and hosted rendering.
landing.pricing.faq.free.question: What is included in the Free plan?
landing.pricing.faq.free.answer: Free includes scene planning, generated Manim code, and three curated models. New accounts also start with free credits you can spend on hosted renders. The Free plan itself does not add recurring render credits.
landing.pricing.faq.pro.question: How do Starter and Pro differ?
landing.pricing.faq.pro.answer: On monthly billing, Starter includes three curated models and 300 render credits; Pro includes all seven models, automatic model fallback, and 1,000 credits. Annual billing grants 3,600 or 12,000 credits for the year. AI output still needs review.
landing.pricing.faq.billing.question: Are Starter and Pro subscriptions?
landing.pricing.faq.billing.answer: Yes. Both have monthly and yearly billing. Manage or cancel an active plan from Settings → Billing; cancellation stops the next renewal.
landing.pricing.faq.code.question: Can I use the generated Manim code outside CurvG?
landing.pricing.faq.code.answer: Yes. You can copy or download the generated Python code. Running it on your own computer still requires a compatible Manim environment and any dependencies used by the scene.
landing.pricing.faq.rendering.question: How are hosted renders calculated?
landing.pricing.faq.rendering.answer: The current standard render costs 20 credits. That makes 300 credits about 15 renders and 1,000 credits about 50. Failed or canceled renders are refunded; estimates update if the cost per render changes.

pages.tool.h1: An online math animation tool that shows its work
pages.tool.lead: CurvG runs in the browser end to end: describe what you want to explain, review the proposed scene plan and Manim code, then render the video in the cloud. No Python, FFmpeg, or LaTeX to install — and the code leaves with you.

pages.tool.faq1_q: Do I need to install anything to use this math animation tool?
pages.tool.faq1_a: No. Planning, code generation, and rendering all run in the browser and the cloud. You only need a local Manim environment if you want to run the exported code on your own machine.
pages.tool.faq2_q: Can I change the animation before it renders?
pages.tool.faq2_a: Yes — that's the point of the workflow. Edit the scene plan directly or ask for a revision in plain language; code regenerates from the approved plan before any render starts.
pages.tool.faq3_q: What do I get at the end?
pages.tool.faq3_a: A rendered MP4 you can download, plus the Manim Community Python code behind it. Both stay attached to your project history.
